name: 3 Series
description: Everyone in a circle. Pick a category (e.g. make of cars, girls names, kinds of food, kinds of plants, whatever).

name: 3 some
description: Fun warm-up. One player offers something, e.g. I am a slice of cheese.

name: Accepting Circle
description: Get everyone in a big circle. One player starts by making a little gesture, perhaps with a little sound.

name: Actor's Nightmare
description: This one is played by 2 players, one of which gets their lines on paper (like a script).

name: Adjective Scene
description: Ask for an adjective (e.g. sad). Play a scene in which the players are as sad as possible.

name: Aerobics
description: This is a fun observation game. Place all players in a line.

name: Ali Baba and the 40 Thieves
description: Excellent warm-up. Everyone in a circle.

name: Alien Tiger Cow
description: Fun game to warm up and to teach players some Chivalry.

name: Alliteration Introduction
description: Excellent game for players to get to know each other's names.

name: Alliterations
description: You will need a tennis ball or a towel tied in a knot for this one.

name: Alphabet Circle
description: Great warm-up game to sharpen concentration. Everyone in a circle.

name: Alphabet Game
description: This is a scene consisting of 26 lines of dialog.

name: American Idol
description: This is a spoof of the format of (American) Idol, the TV show in which new singers are discovered.

name: Animalistics
description: Ask the audience for animals. Players play a scene, in which the characters are based on these animals.

name: Animals
description: Make sure you have an even number of players.

name: Artist Model Clay
description: 3 players. One is a lump of clay - behind her is a second player who is a model.

name: Asides
description: A scene is played, which any player can stop at any time by yelling freeze.

name: Assassin
description: Great warm-up for a group of 7+ people. Everyone picks someone to be their bodyguard, and somebody to be their assassin.

name: Association Jump
description: This is physical association game. All plays mill about the room.

name: Audience Warm-ups
description: Often an improvised show starts with an audience warm-up.

name: Automatic Storytelling
description: This is an exercise you can only do once with a group.

name: Back Dancing
description: Played in pairs. Actors stand back to back, and dance on different kinds of music.

name: Backwards Interview
description: Ask for a topic for a TV interview. Then 2 players do the interview backwards.

name: Balladeer(1)
description: One player is the balladeer, who starts singing a ballad about an audience suggestion.

name: Balladeer(2)
description: This is like the short form version Balladeer, but now as soon as the balladeer stops singing or finishes the song, the characters start playing and talking independently.

name: Barney
description: Silly warm-up game. Everyone in a circle, one person as a 'caller' in the middle.

name: BarPro
description: The (slightly negative sounding) name is attributed to Keith Johnstone and refers to shows consisting of short games, played in small rooms, like bars and tiny comedy clubs.

name: Bartender
description: Ask for a silly problem. Player 1 goes into a bar and explains his woes to the bartender in a song.

name: Beatnik Poet
description: Tell the audience we are going to improvise a bad poetry night at pseudo- intellectual coffee house.

name: Become
description: This one can be player with all players at a time, or you can ask the group to watch as players come up with different ideas on how to do this.

name: Before or After
description: A short scene is played. After that the host asks the audience whether they want to see what happened before this scene, or what happens after this scene.

name: Bidirectional Satellite TV
description: Fairly difficult combination of Satellite TV and Satellite Radio: players in pairs, establish a beat.

name: Big Blob
description: Players perform a scene in a location that contains an enormous blob of blubber.

name: Big Booty
description: Everyone in a circle. One player is Big Booty.

name: Big Fish Small Fish
description: Fun energizer game. Everyone in a circle.

name: Bippety Bop(1)
description: Silly warm-up to get the blood flowing. A players in a circle, one player in the middle.

name: Bippety Bop(2)
description: This is a variation on Bippety Bop: all players in a circle, one player in the middle who is 'it'.

name: Black Box
description: This one is played by 2 players. One holds a (mimed) black box, which has 3 buttons, one of which is red.

name: Blind Association Circle
description: This one starts just like Free Association Circle: players in a circle, establish a rhythm, and freely associate on previous player's word.

name: Blindfolded Scene
description: Players are blindfolded and then play a scene.

name: Blind Freeze
description: This one is just like Freeze Tag, but here the MC calls Freeze, and calls in another player.

name: Blind Harold
description: This is really a listening exercise, though it has been performed as a Long Form for audiences.

name: Blind Lead
description: One player is blindfolded, and the room is filled with obstacles (put a couple of chairs everywhere, leave all kinds of junk on the floor).

name: Blind Line Offers
description: Line up the players, give'em each a number. Call out 2 numbers.

name: Blind Line Up
description: This one is like Group Order, except that everyone keeps their eyes closed, and no talking is allowed while the group lines up.

name: Blind Musical
description: This is like a musical version of Pockets: ask the audience to write simple sentences on slips of paper.

name: Blues Jam
description: Ask the audience for 5 things that give them the blues.

name: Body Hide
description: Excellent exercise to get to know each other, and to learn to trust and touch each other.

name: Bong Bong Bong
description: Silly game, inspired by a Korean TV show (so we're told).

name: Boris
description: 2 players play an interrogation scene. One is the interrogator, the other is a suspect.

name: Bucket
description: Before the show ask the audience to write simple sentences on slips of paper.

name: Bunny
description: Extremely silly game, to pump up the energy. Get everyone in a circle.

name: Call from Ray
description: A scene is begun. At some point in the scene an onstage player has to receive a "Call from Ray" (or any other name agreed upon).

name: Cards
description: Ask the audience to write short sentences on cards.

name: Card Status
description: Excellent Status game. 4 players.

name: Cat and Mouse
description: All players in pairs. One player is cat, one other player is mouse, and all others stay in pairs, arms hooked together.

name: Catch'em
description: One player is 'it' and stands at one end of the room, facing the wall.

name: Circle of Knots
description: Form a circle, holding hands. Then, any player can start moving about, making knots in the circle.

name: Circle Sitting
description: Have everyone stand in a circle, really close to each other, facing inwards.

name: Clap Snap Association
description: This one is like a Free Association Circle, except that the rhythm is more explicit.

name: Clap Snap Stamp
description: All players in pairs, facing each other. We're going to count from one to three, each player one number at a time, and we keep repeating this.

name: Click Bang you're dead
description: Description: all players sit in a circle. Only one player should know how to play and what the secret is; this player is the leader at first, until others catch on.

name: Columbian Hypnosis
description: Played in pairs. One player holds her open hand, fingers upward, about 2-3 inches from her partner's face.

name: ComedySportz
description: ComedySports was started by Dick Chudnow in 1884 in Milwaukee.

name: Coming Home
description: Ask players to think of someone they know. Then ask them to play how that person would come home from work.

name: Commercial
description: Ask for a product (existing or non-existing).

name: Complete Bodies
description: Players in pairs. One player takes a position, using all parts of her body.

name: Concentration Circle
description: Place all players in a circle and number them sequentially, starting with a random player.

name: Confessions
description: Not exactly theater but fun when played well.

name: Continuing Emotions
description: A 'neutral' scene is started, and is then interrupted (frozen) several times by the MC.

name: Continuing Styles
description: A 'neutral' scene is started. This scene gets interrupted several times by the MC, and then continued in a film/ literature/ drama/ TV-program style provided by the audience.

name: CopyCat
description: CopyCat goes like a verbal Freeze Tag. A scene is started.

name: Crabtrees Conundrum
description: This game is taking from Mrs. Crabtree from South Park.

name: Crime Endowments
description: One player is endowed as the head of a criminal organization and gathers with the others to plan or act out the crime.

name: Crisis Situation
description: Great exercise for spontaneity. 2 players on stage approach each other with a crisis, and an object unrelated to the crisis.

name: Cross Circle
description: Perfect game to learn each other's names. Everyone in a circle.

name: Cut
description: This Long Form game is played with 6 to 15 players.

name: Dating Game
description: This is played like a Blind Date show. One player leaves the stage, and the audience provides endowments for the 3 others.

name: Day in the Life
description: The MC picks a member of the audience and interviews this person about their average (work) day.

name: Deaf Replay
description: 2 players play a scene while 2 others watch the scene, with their ears covered.

name: Death and Retriever
description: This one is like Scorpion, but in this version killed players are not 'out', but can be revived.

name: Death in a Minute
description: 2 or 3 players play a 1 minute scene, in which one player must die.

name: Diamond
description: 4 players in a square; 2 in front, 2 behind them.

name: Ding Characters
description: This is like Ding: players play a scene. When a bell is rang, they both need to drop into a completely different character, but the scene continues.

name: Ding Dong
description: This is a variation on Day in the Life: pick an audience member and ask her some questions about her day.

name: Ding
description: A scene is played. Whenever the MC ring a bell (or yells 'Ding'), the player that is doing something/saying something needs to say/do something else.

name: Director's Cut
description: A normal scene is played. At any moment a player not in the scene (or a player dedicated to this particular role) stops the scene (see Cut) and has the actors replay the scene with different...

name: Disc(1)
description: Tell the players to imagine the stage is a disc, only supported right in the center of the stage.

name: Disc(2)
description: Imagine the stage is a large disc, supported in the middle.

name: Dissociation
description: This game can be done individually, or you can have one player do it in front of the class.

name: Distance Game
description: Two players stand a few feet apart facing each other and have the most boring 4-line interchange possible.

name: Distorting Mirror
description: This is a variation of the classic Mirror exercise.

name: Doors
description: Excellent introductory exercise for building environments and Platform.

name: Doo Wop(1)
description: This is another structured song format, sung as a 1950's doo-wop.

name: Doo Wop(2)
description: This is another structured long form. Get a topic, line up the players, and start improvising a song around the theme, usually without using a piano player (it would get too structured and...

name: Do Ron Ron
description: 4 players sing a song about a subject, given by the audience, on the tune of Do Ron Ron.

name: Double Blind Freeze
description: This is an extension of Blind Freeze: 2 players in scene, the others line up with their backs to the scene.

name: Double Endowment
description: Another great game to train listening skills.

name: Double Opening
description: 2 players each make a (strong) opening sentence, at the same time.

name: Dry Cleaning Bag of Death
description: We need three or four players. During the scene, one player is always off-stage, with his head inside a dry cleaning bag, slowly suffocating.

name: Dubbed Movie
description: 2 or more actors play a scene, but they don't speak, although they can move their mouths as if they are speaking.

name: Duck Duck Goose
description: Invent a name for a non-existing but simple children's game.

name: DVD Special Edition
description: Start off with a trailer, narrated by one of the players, followed by some quick scenes, maximum 5 lines per scene.

name: Eights
description: Excellent game to warm up those muscles. Everybody scatter around, stand up relaxedly.

name: Elephant
description: This one is like an extended version of Bippety Bop.

name: Emotional Family
description: Usually played with 4 players, but can be done with more or less players.

name: Emotional Mirror
description: Players in pairs, facing each other. One starts talking in gibberish, with a specific emotion (angry, happy, in love, you name it).

name: Emotional Quadrants
description: Divide the scene in 4 quadrants, and allocate 4 different emotions to each quadrant.

name: Emotions Characters
description: Players in pairs, arms loosely hanging (not folded, not stuck in pant pockets).

name: Endowments
description: This is a general handle for a ton of endowment games: one player leaves, the audience gives an occupation, and this player need to be endowed with that occupation.

name: Energy 1-10
description: Everyone in a big circle, squatting down. We will count 1 to 10, all together, moving up, with increasing energy level.

name: Evil Stick of Gum
description: This is a variation on Little Voice. In this game one character has a piece of gum in her mouth, and this piece of gum is capable of talking.

name: Evil Twin
description: 4 players. 2 will play a scene.

name: Exaggeration Circle
description: All players in a circle, or a long line. One player starts a little gesture, with or without a little sound..

name: Excluding
description: 4 players play a scene, in which one of the players gets excluded.

name: Family Portraits
description: Fun game to get everyone to work together. Players are going to 'build' family portraits.

name: Famous Last Words
description: MC asks the audience for famous (living or dead) people, or characters in movies, cartoons or songs.

name: Famous Person Endowment
description: 1 player gets a number of famous persons; one for each other player in the scene.

name: Fast Food Laban
description: Laban was a movement theorist, and this exercise is based on (a simplified form of some of) his ideas.

name: Fast Food Stanislawski
description: Have 2 players perform a scene, perhaps give them a title or a location, but also give them a subtext for their character.

name: Fast Forward
description: For this handle we need a 'director', or the MC can take on this role.

name: Feature Film
description: This is a collection of scenes, all based around (the making of) a movie.

name: Final Freeze
description: This is an extension of Blind Freeze: players try to do callbacks from previous scenes in the Freeze.

name: Finger Applause
description: Have the audience clap not their hands, but start with 2 fingers.

name: Fingertips
description: Played in pairs. Players touch all ten fingers, and one player closes her eyes.

name: Firing Squad
description: This is an association game, sometimes used in workshops to 'punish' a silly or inattentive student.

name: Five Four Three Two One
description: This is a long format, origin unknown, and has resemblance to a Harold.

name: Five Things
description: One player leaves the stage while the Host asks for an everyday activity.

name: Flock Dance
description: This is a physical warm-up. The group forms a pyramid: one player becomes the top, 2 players behind her, 3 players on a third line, and so on.

name: Follow the Leader
description: All but one in a circle, one player in the middle.

name: Follow your Nose
description: Silly physical warm-up. Have everybody mill around the room, and shout a body part.

name: Foreign Movie
description: 2 players play a story in Gibberish, 2 others translate.

name: Fortune Cookie
description: Open a fortune cookie, read it aloud. Then play a scene based on the fortune.

name: Fortune Teller
description: One player covers his ears while the others get 'predictions' from the audience; one prediction per other player.

name: Free Association Circle
description: Everyone in a circle and we establish a rhythm, by swinging a hand.

name: Free Association
description: This is the classic association exercise. There are various ways of playing this (see Variations and see other games in the Association category.

name: Free Association Lines
description: Yet another way to play association games. Place all players on 2 lines, facing each other.

name: Free Falling
description: Nice, but a bit dangerous exercise to build trust.

name: French Braid
description: This is a very simple format, which consists of a number of (unrelated) scenes, that get interrupted, and then continues at a later point.

name: Front Desk
description: We play a scene, set in the lobby of a hotel.

name: Fruit Basket
description: All players but one sitting a circle, one person in the middle.

name: Fusillade
description: Great exercise in fast thinking, but seen done in performance as well.

name: Fuzzy Ducky
description: Silly concentration game and great warm-up. All players in a circle.

name: Game-O-Matic
description: This is like 'invent-your-won-game': ask the audience for the name of an unexisting improv game, then invent the rules on the spot, and play it.

name: Gibberish Commands
description: Another exercise on Jabbertalk: players in pairs.

name: Gibberish Expert
description: One player is an expert on a subject, often provided by the audience.

name: Gibberish Malapropism
description: This exercise flexes your mind and is a good exercise for Gibberish games.

name: Give and Take
description: This is a variation on Walking by Numbers: all players find a position the room.

name: Goalie
description: Great high-tempo exercise. 1 player up front.

name: Goon River
description: This is a format that consists of monologues.

name: Gorilla Theatre
description: This format is played with 3 experienced players, one MC and another player, dressed up as a Gorilla.

name: Greetings
description: All players start milling about the room. You then ask them to greet each other, perhaps just by shaking hands.

name: Group Environment
description: This is a group exercise in building environments.

name: Group Freeze
description: Everyone starts milling about the room. Any player may decide to stop walking at any time.

name: Group Order
description: Nice warm-up exercise to help the group function/agree as a whole.

name: Guest Game
description: In this game we play in scene in which one player is a guest, somewhere.

name: Hall of Justice
description: Fun game for 5+ players, involving superheroes and villains.

name: Handicapped Fairy Tale
description: Very silly but very effective. Ask the audience for a fairy tale.

name: Hand Slap
description: All players in a circle, down on the floor. Cross arms, and then put hands flat on the ground.

name: Hat Continuation
description: Start a scene, and identify each of the characters by means of a hat.

name: Hats
description: A very silly game. 2 improvisers put on hats, preferably similarly sized.

name: Heave Ho
description: This is like an extended version of Tossing to be played with 16+ players.

name: Helping Hands
description: Scene played by 4 players, playing 2 characters.

name: He Said She Said
description: Excellent game to show how Endowment works. 2 players; each player will state the action the other player must perform, followed by his own line.

name: Hesitation
description: In this game a scene is played, in which at any time, any player may 'hesitate', and ask the audience for help.

name: Hijacker
description: Excellent game to train listening skills. 4 players, one leaves the room.

name: Hitch Hiker
description: Use 4 chairs to build the interior of a car. One player starts driving the car, and another player becomes a hitch hiker, hiking a ride.

name: Honey Walk
description: This is a group exercise. Tell the players they have an oxygen mask, and then talk them thru the exercise: players are to move about in successively thicker substances.

name: Horoscope
description: Take a magazine with a horoscope. Ask an audience member for their birthday, read their horoscope and then play a scene based on that horoscope.

name: Hot Spot
description: All players in a circle. One player steps into the circle and starts singing a known song.

name: Human Props
description: Excellent exercise for building environments.

name: ID
description: Ask a number of Ids, driver's licences from audience members.

name: I Love You
description: A simple song structure for 2 singers. Singer 1 sings 4 lines; the first 3 are about the other character; line 4 is simply "I love you".

name: Imitate
description: This is an exercise for characters. 2 players will play a scene in a shop.

name: Impro Match
description: This format does not have a specific name and is mainly popular in French speaking countries.

name: In-Out
description: Every player gets a word from the audience. When that word is said by any player, this player must leave the scene if he's in it, or enter the scene if he was not in it (yet).

name: Introducing Association
description: This little technique can be used to show a new group how natural associating really is.

name: Invisibility
description: Scene in which one oe the characters in invisible to the audience.

name: Invocation
description: This is a kind of Opening for Long Form. It goes in three steps.

name: Irish Drinking Song
description: 4 players sing a song about a subject, given by the audience, on an Irish-souding tune, one line at a time.

name: Janus Dance
description: This is can be used as a Trust exercise, as well as in performance.

name: Jeopardy
description: This games is not unlike Worlds Worst: have the players close/cover their ears.

name: Jump
description: This is at times a physical Warm-up, a physical association game, and a game for character work.

name: Just Gibberish
description: Excellent exercise for players that suffer from chronic Waffling.

name: Killer Bunny
description: This is like Bunny except that at any time, the middle bunny is allowed to lift her hands above her head, lunge to either right or left side and eat one of her own ears, after which the ear player...

name: King Game
description: One player is the king or the queen. Other players are to try and pleas his/her Royal Highness.

name: Kitty in the Corner
description: Classic children's game. 4 to 6 players stand at corners of the playing area, one player in the middle.

name: Ksss
description: Nice warm-up, easier to play than to explain.

name: Last Letter
description: This is an Association game, where instead of naming the first word you think of upon hearing a previous word, you name the first word you think of starting with the last letter of the previously...

name: Last Letter Scene
description: A scene is played, in which every next line spoken needs to start with the last letter of the previous line.

name: Last Line
description: Get a line (any line) from the audience. Players play a scene that concludes with the given line.

name: LCD
description: This game is called Location, Career, Death (LCD).

name: Lets Not
description: Excellent game to train narrative skills, but a bit controversial.

name: Letter Number Name
description: Warm-up game that's also good to get to know each other's names.

name: Line Mirror
description: This is an extension of the Mirror game. Have all players line up in two face-to face rows, about three feet apart, holding hands (within a row).

name: Little Voice
description: One player plays a scene. The other player(s) play the voice(s) of objects in the environment in which the first player plays.

name: Location
description: Get a location (say the Post Office). The whole long form is played in one and the same Post Office.

name: Lotus
description: This is just a series of scenes in which each new scene evolves out of the dynamics of the previous scene.

name: Lounge Singer
description: Ask for an unlikely place to find a lounge singer.

name: Machines
description: MC/trainer comes up with a (real or invented) machine.

name: Make More Interesting
description: Simple exercise, useful for players that are too verbal.

name: Making Faces
description: ' A silly handle attributed to Keith Johnstone.

name: Malapropism
description: This game flexes your mind. Have the players walk about in the room, point to any object, and give it another name.

name: Man Overboard
description: This is a nice elimination warm-up. Everyone spreads out in a staggered line, like in an aerobics class.

name: Mantra
description: Let the players play a short scene. Then ask them to repeat the following mantra in their head, and replay the scene 'I'm so happy, I'm so happy'.

name: Mantra Introduction
description: Here's a way to make a point about blanking one's mind, subconscious thinking and spontaneity.

name: Marriage Counsel Endowment
description: One player is sent out of the room while the host gets 2 relationship problems from the audience.

name: Marshmallow Mania
description: Play a scene in which the audience is not supposed to laugh.

name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
description: Begin with 2 players, each on a chair. In character they start to talk about what happened to them in the past.

name: Massage
description: Place all players in a circle. Have everyone put their hands on their right neighbor's shoulders and give 'em a shoulder massage.

name: Master Servant Disaster
description: 2 players, one is the master, the other is the servant.

name: Mega Replay
description: Divide the players in 2 groups. A scene is played by the first group from a well known story, fairy tale, historic fact.

name: Mexican Name Wave
description: Players in a circle. Let them do a Mexican Wave: one player lifts both arms in the air, and down again.

name: Micetro
description: Pronounce as 'Maestro'. Comparable to Gorilla Theatre, but a bit easier, and can be played with a fairly large number of players (up to 20), and 2 directors.

name: Millipede
description: Great fun but be careful not to hurt each other.

name: More or Less
description: This is a nice show format. Any number of players from 5 upwards.

name: Move and Speak
description: Play a 2-player scene, in which no-one is allowed to talk unless they create a new object and a movement along with it.

name: Movie Review
description: 4-10 players. Ask the audience for a movie title.

name: Mr. So and So
description: This is a game that's more suited for rehearshal than for performance, though I can work on stage as well.

name: My Fault
description: You need 2 plastic bottles, each with a little bit of water (not too much or they'd be too heavy).

name: Name 6 Circle
description: You will need a tennis ball or a towel tied in a knot for this one.

name: Name the Monster
description: Play in pairs, one word at a time (see Word at a Time Scene).

name: Name Volley
description: Divide the class into 2 groups, maximum 6 players per group.

name: No Doubles 1-10
description: Nice concentration game. Everyone in a circle.

name: Non Sequitor
description: Place players in pairs, let them hold a casual conversation about their work, the weather, anything.

name: No P
description: Players play a scene (perhaps based on an audience suggestion) but they cannot use the letter 'P' (or any other letter).

name: Nuclear Bomb Chicken
description: You can do this only once with a new group. Tell them they are all chickens in a henhouse, and a nuclear bomb is about to drop on the henhouse within 30 seconds, Ask the players to play the...

name: Object Morphing
description: Good exercise on object work: players in pairs.

name: Object Narrative
description: Place one chair on stage. The group sits or stands to the sides so they can see what is going on.

name: Objects
description: Divide the class in 2 groups. Give one group the name of an object, and they become, as a group, the object.

name: Old Job New Job
description: Play a scene with 2 players, and give them a job (or let the audience provide the job).

name: One Duck
description: Everyone in a circle. We are going to say a pattern, one word per player, going clockwise.

name: One Eighty Five
description: Not really improv theater but done by a quite a few troupes, and fun when done well.

name: One Line Scene
description: Play a one or two minute scene, where only one line of dialog can be spoken.

name: One Mouth
description: One player (or the MC) is going to interview all other players, but the group of other players are really one character.

name: One Two Three Four
description: Ok, this is harder to explain than it is to play.

name: Only Questions
description: A scene is played, in which any sentence used by the players must be a question.

name: Open Offer
description: One player starts a scene by making an offer that is not 'complete', in the sense that it is vague enough not to define the who/what/where right away.

name: Open Your Hand
description: Let the players walk around the room leisurely.

name: Opposite Characters
description: This is basically the opposite to Imitate: for the shopkeeper, rather than imitating the customer's character, try and build a totally opposite character.

name: Opposites
description: Let the players walk around the room in silence.

name: Overload
description: Excellent exercise to train listening skills by means of sensory overload.

name: Parallel Universe
description: Audience provides 2 different environments/locations.

name: Pass Ball
description: All players in a circle. Ask the players to pass a mimed ball to others (one ball at a time).

name: Pass Clap
description: Classic warm-up. Everyone in a circle.

name: Pass Yes
description: This is a bit like Pass Clap and all it's variations.

name: Patterns
description: This is a bit like Free Association Circle, except that player are not to freely associate on the previously heard word, but on the ensemble of what has been heard, thereby heightening is.

name: Pecking Order
description: Every player picks a number between 1 and the number of players in the scene.

name: Peruvian Ball Game
description: Everyone starts milling about the room, miming a particular kind of ball.

name: Pillars
description: Put one member of the audience on stage (the pillar).

name: Play Tag
description: Just play tag. Excellent physical warm-up.

name: Pockets
description: Before the show, ask the audience to write simple sentences on slips of paper.

name: Poetry Corner
description: You may want to practice this one: 1 player starts with the first line of a poem; player 2 adds second line, and so forth.

name: Poet Translator
description: A simple translation game. The setup is a foreign language poet, who performs some of his work in Gibberish.

name: Point of View
description: Play a simple scene. Then the scene is replayed, from the point of view of one of the characters.

name: Popcorn
description: Everyone finds themselves a nice spot, and squat down.

name: Presents
description: Great warm-up exercise that helps you blank your mind.

name: Press Conference
description: 3 to 8 players. One player leaves the room, while the audience provides the name of a famous or historical person.

name: Primal Screams
description: All players in a circle. On player steps into the circle, making a big gesture and a loud sound.

name: Props
description: In this game the players need to come up with an original/funny use of a prop.

name: Protest Song
description: Ask the audience for something that pisses them off.

name: Puppets
description: 4 players. 2 players will be puppets; these players offer the lines of dialog in the scene, but they are not allowed to move about themselves.

name: Rash
description: Make sure you have as many pieces of paper as there are players.

name: Real Estate Broker
description: One player is a real estate broker and shows a second player (or multiple players) around a space, given by the audience/trainer.

name: Receiver Right Clap
description: Nice concentration and warmup exercise. All players in a circle.

name: Repair Shop
description: One player leaves the stage (or gets a headphone).

name: Repeater
description: Listening exercise. Any player that wants to offer a piece of dialog needs to repeat the entire dialog the last player did (ignoring that player's repetition of previous dialog) before she can...

name: Replay Gibberish
description: Exercise on Jabbertalk. Have 2 players do a short scene (1 minute or so).

name: Reverse Chair Dance
description: You will need music for this exercise; provide a tape deck or a ghetto blaster, and a bunch of chairs.

name: Reverse Trivial Pursuit
description: Like most of the games in the Verbal wit category, no exactly theater, but fun if played well.

name: Rhymes
description: Scene played in verses. The idea is that the first player offers a line, and the second player rhymes to that.

name: Rituals
description: Get an everyday activity from the audience. Then play this activity as if it were a ritual.

name: Rumors
description: Everyone in a circle. One person starts by saying "Did you hear about..." and points to someone else.

name: Samurai
description: This is an excellent physical warm up. All players in a circle.

name: Satellite Radio
description: Excellent listening exercise. Players in pairs.

name: Satellite TV
description: Same as Satellite Radio, but with movements. Players in pairs.

name: Scene in the Dark
description: Fairly obvious: a scene is played in the dark.

name: Scene Painting
description: Technique for building/advancing scenes. To be used sparingly.

name: Scene Replay
description: Ask 2 players to play a short scene. One could limit the scene to 8 lines of dialog per player.

name: Scene To Music
description: A silent scene is played, in which the characters' emotions are controlled by the music.

name: Scorpion
description: A number of players stand in the middle of the room, eyes closed the others stand by the walls.

name: Sculptors
description: Works best with an even number of players. Split the group in 2.

name: Seven Up
description: Everyone in a circle, start counting to 7 while waving right arm up and down to the same rhythm you're counting.

name: Shootout
description: Excellent game to get to know each other's names.

name: Sideways
description: In this game we play a scene, in which the back wall is the 'floor', and the floor is a wall.

name: Silly Stinky Sexy
description: 4 players. Each player endows each of the other players with either sexy-ness, silly-ness or stinky-ness.

name: Simon Says
description: You are Simon, and you tell the players to do exactly what Simon tells them to do, but only if Simon's sentence starts with "Simon says".

name: Simple Continuation
description: A scene is started, played by 2 to 4 players.

name: Sitting Standing Lying
description: Silly game to teach fast acting. 3 players play a scene.

name: Six Episodes
description: Excellent game to teach group storytelling. Give a big task, like 'The launch of a new flavor of coke', or 'Building a new clubhouse for the girl scouts'.

name: Slappy Face
description: A simple word association played in pairs. If a player is too slow, of goed 'Erm...' the other slaps him in the face (gently).

name: Slap Take
description: Very silly. But hey we're an encyclopedia; some folks really do this on stage, so here we go: 2 players do a scene.

name: Slide Show
description: Give one player a big activity, perhaps a trip through the jungle, or the construction of a home.

name: SloMo Samurai
description: Tell the players they are Samurai, and their right forearm is a poisoned sword.

name: SloMo Tag
description: Play tag, but in slow motion. Immensely entertaining if played well; players are not to escape the tagger by making a sudden movement, and the tagger cannot lash out to tag another player.

name: Soap Series
description: Play an episode from a soap series. This can be done as a Long Form, but can also be used in short form.

name: Solitaire
description: All players but one spread along opposing edges of a wide surface.

name: Solo Doors
description: A Solo exercise. Enter, as a character, through a door.

name: Sound Circle
description: Everybody in a big circle. One player starts the game by making a gesture and a sound to his right neighbor.

name: Sound Effects
description: A scene is played, and one or more off-scene players provide all the sounds.

name: Sounds Like a Song
description: Play a scene (or series of scenes). At any time, anyone can stop the scene and say 'Sounds like a song', after which the player(s) sing a song based on the last line that was spoken, or last...

name: Space Jump
description: This is like an extended Freeze Tag game. 4 players.

name: Spit Take
description: Very silly. But hey we're an encyclopedia so here we go: 2 players do a scene, each holding a glass of water (or coke, or beer).

name: Split Screen
description: Divide the stage in a left and a right half. The right part becomes the left and vice versa, and the division in the middle becomes a 'wall'.

name: Sportz Center
description: 3 players, and an every day activity (brushing your teeth, washing your car).

name: Squeezer
description: Get everyone into a circle, holding hands. One player starts the game by squeezing the hand of one of his neighbors.

name: Story Spine
description: This is an idea about the spine of any story.

name: Story Story Die
description: Players form a line on the stage. A title for a story, and a story genre is obtained from the audience.

name: Story To A Chair
description: A Solo character exercise. Tell a story to a few chairs.

name: Stretching
description: As a warm-up, let's do some simple stretching exercises.

name: Stunt Double
description: A scene is played by 2 players. Every time a player needs to do something difficult/unpleasant, another player jumps in as a stunt double.

name: Sung Story Die
description: This is like Story Story Die, but sung. Get a suggestions, and sing a song to that suggestion.

name: Superman Jam
description: Divide the audience into three groups; label them Group 1, 2, 3, (or any other labeling).

name: Supermen
description: A great Pimping game. 4 players.

name: Supernova
description: Nice energy builder. All players dispersed around the room, have everyone stand up comfortably, feet apart, eyes closed.

name: Surprise Movement
description: Have everyone walk around leisurely. Tel them to stop and start make a movement, a gesture, a sound, anything really.

name: Survivor
description: Four to six players play a scene. Then the audience chooses one of the players to get "voted off the island." The remaining players do the scene again, covering everything that happened the first...

name: Swedish Sculptors
description: This one is an extension of Sculptors. Divide the class in 2 groups, same number of players in every group.

name: Switcheroo
description: This is like Simple Continuation, except that the MC interrupts the scene several times, and at each interruption all actors in the scene get switched; no new actors join in, and no actors leave.

name: Switch Gibberish
description: Jabbertalk exercise: let a player tell a store.

name: Sybil
description: This is basically a one-person Long Form. In this format the player plays all characters.

name: Synchro Clap
description: All players in a circle. One player starts the game by making eye contact with another player.

name: TellTales
description: In this format a cast of five gets one ask-for each at the top of the show, and then each person is free to play solo scenes with invisible characters, addressing the audience, musing to...

name: Theatresports
description: Theatre Sports is really a collection of formats.

name: The Bag
description: This is a group exercise for building Characters.

name: The Bat
description: This is a Long Form format based on Blind Harold.

name: The Gerbil
description: Invent a silly dramatic story, and explain it to the audience.

name: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly Advice
description: 3 players, form a line (or sit down). The audience provides questions or problems for which they need advice.

name: The Magnet
description: Played in pairs. One player becomes a sculpture, standing still, while his partner closes her eyes.

name: The Party
description: One player plays a character that is having a party.

name: The Scream
description: Everybody in a circle, watch the ground. On your sign, everybody lifts their head and either looks straight, left or right.

name: Three Line Environment
description: Played with 2 players. They get 3 lines (first player gets 2 lines, second one gets one line).

name: Three Line Solo
description: This is a Solo exercise. Play a 3 line scene with 2 characters.

name: Three Melodies
description: Ask for 2 occupations. Then do a 4-beat scene as follows: Player 1 sings about how great and satisfying her job is, but she's missing something critical, or

name: Three Noses
description: A fun and silly game. Let everyone walk leisurely around the room.

name: Three Rules
description: Get 3 rules from the audience, e.g. players have only one arm, players can't use a word that contains an's' and after every question uttered players needs to yell 'Yess!'.

name: Three Sentence Story
description: 2 players. 3 unconnected sentences are provided by one player; the other builds the shortest possible story incorporating the 3 sentences.

name: Timed Scenes
description: Here are a couple of different ways to time scenes (apart from using your watch) time a player can keep his head immersed in a bucket of water

name: Timeline
description: A scene is played, number of players unlimited.

name: Tossing
description: Eight players form 2 lines, facing each other, and mesh their forearms together, to form a platform to 'launch' another player up in the air and catch him again.

name: Touch to Talk
description: In this handle players play a scene in which they can only use speech when they touch each other.

name: Translate Gibberish
description: This is best played with an odd number of players.

name: Translation for the Deaf
description: We need 3 players for this game. One will be an expert on a topic provided by the audience; another will be the interviewer.

name: Triple Play
description: This is really a series of 3 3-act plays mixed.

name: Trivial Pursuit
description: MC asks the audience to pick Trivial Pursuit cards.

name: Tug-O-War
description: Divide the class in 2 groups and have them mime a Tug-o-war fight.

name: Turning Circle
description: Fun game to warm up those muscles and get the blood pumping.

name: TV News
description: 3 players, who play characters in a TV newscast.

name: Typewriter
description: This is a nice handle to structure scenes. One of the players is the Narrator.

name: Verses
description: Scene is played in verses, that is, every player need to rhyme to herself.

name: Virus
description: Use one empty plastic soft drink bottle. Whichever player has the bottle is the virus.

name: Voices From Heaven
description: Excellent game for building characters and group-storytelling.

name: Walking by Numbers
description: Every player finds himself a spot in the room, make sure players can see each other.

name: Walkout
description: You need at least 3 players for this one. Give each player a word.

name: Walk-over Association
description: Another way of playing association games. Place all players at one end of the room.

name: Warehouse
description: Let the players walk around leisurely. Tell them they are in a big warehouse, with lots of shelves and cabinets, packed with junk.

name: What Happens Next
description: One player in the middle, the others sit aside.

name: What Has Changed
description: Played in pairs. One player observes another closely.

name: What would she be if
description: Choose one player and let her stand in front of the class.

name: Whoosh
description: Everybody in a circle. Start with one person, who waves both hands to his/her neighbor, saying 'Whoosh'.

name: Who Where Why Am I
description: One player leaves the room. The audience provides: where we are, and when (what era)

name: Without Sound
description: A scene in played, in which no talk of no sounds are allowed.

name: Without Words
description: A scene is played, in which the players are not allowed to talk.

name: Word at a Time Expert
description: 3 players: one is the interviewer, and the other 2 are an expert on a subject chosen by the audience.

name: Word at a Time Letter
description: Play in pairs. The 2 players will compose a letter, one word at a time.

name: Word at a Time Scene
description: This is like Word at a Time Expert, but with a bit more scene work.

name: Word at a Time Song
description: This is like Word at a Time Scene, but here the players improvise a song.

name: Word at a Time Story
description: This is an exercise to train group narrative.

name: Word Ball
description: Another association game. All players in a circle.

name: Worlds Worst
description: Not exactly theater, but fun if played well. Players line up, and the audience provides verbs, hobbies and occupations.

name: Yes Lets - or Rather Not
description: This is a bit controversial, and you probably don't want to do this with newbies.

name: You
description: Everyone in a circle. Everyone raises their right hand.

name: You're Fired
description: This is a scene with 2 players, in which the lines are scripted.

name: Zapping
description: 4 players, each chooses a TV format, like the News, a documentary, a Pokemon show, you name it.

name: Zoom-In Zoom-Out
description: A scene is played; at any time the MC or host calls "zoom-out" - at that point, the scene continues, but is played with finger puppets (as if the audience is watching the scene from fart away, and...

name: Zulu(1)
description: All players form a line, facing the audience.

name: Zulu(2)
description: All players form a line, facing the audience.
